items.title: Malaysia agrees in principle to support Maldives’ US$100m soft loan request, says Anwar
items.summary: MALE, Sept 15 — Malaysia has agreed in principle to support the Maldives’ application for a US$100 million (US$1=RM4.07) financing facility, which Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim described as a form of soft loan to be implemented through both countries’ monetary authorities. Anwar said that the terms and mechanism for the facility are still being worked out by Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and the Maldives Monetary Authority (MMA). “The President has written to me about the need to get our central bank, Bank Negara Malaysia, to respond to the Maldivian request, precisely (from) the Maldives Monetary Authority, for this US$100 million facility.

items.title: Maldives, Malaysia strengthen defence and Islamic cooperation
items.summary: MALÉ: Maldives and Malaysia have strengthened their institutional ties through new cooperation agreements in defence and Islamic affairs, while reaffirming their shared positions on Palestine and climate change. Maldives President Dr Mohamed Muizzu said the agreements witnessed during Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's state visit would open new avenues for practical cooperation between the two countries. "Today, we also witnessed the exchange of new cooperation agreements in two important areas, which are defence cooperation and Islamic faith," he said.

items.title: Indonesia to open trading at planned commodity bourse on January 4, official says
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia plans to start trading at its new commodity exchange on Jan 4, 2027, with tin and ferronickel to be included in the opening transactions, the chief supervisor of the commodity exchange said on Tuesday. Friderica Widyasari Dewi, chairperson of the Financial Services Authority (OJK), said the exchange would help combat under-invoicing and end transfer-pricing practices for commodity exports. "Trading on the mineral and strategic commodity exchange is expected to launch in early January, January 4, 2027, through the ICOMEX entity," Sarjito said, referring to the name of the planned exchange.

items.title: Malaysia raises October crude palm oil reference price, duty remains at 10pct
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has raised its October crude palm oil reference price to a level that maintains the export duty at 10 per cent, a circular on the Malaysian Palm Oil Board website showed on Tuesday. The world's second-largest palm exporter calculated a reference price of 4,452.66 ringgit (US$1,091.34) per tonne for October. The September reference price was 4,392.32 ringgit a tonne, and incurred a duty of 10 per cent.

items.title: YTL Power, Ganda Power secure four additional Siemens Energy gas turbine units
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: YTL Power International Bhd, Ganda Power and Siemens Energy have signed reservation agreements for four additional SGT-9000HL gas turbine units. In a statement issued by YTL Power, the company said the latest reservations bring the total number of units secured by Ganda and YTL Power to seven, including three units obtained earlier. According to YTL Power, Siemens Energy's SGT-9000HL gas turbine family is designed to deliver high efficiency, operational flexibility and reliability, supporting dependable electricity supply as power systems integrate more renewable energy.

items.title: Malaysia to resolve bureaucratic hurdles affecting Maldivian students, healthcare
items.summary: MALÉ: Malaysia will seek to resolve bureaucratic issues affecting Maldivian students and their parents, while strengthening cooperation in healthcare, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar said more than 2,000 Maldivian students were currently studying in Malaysia, reflecting the confidence placed by Maldives in the country's education system. We don't have problems with Maldivians living in Malaysia, working in Malaysia, or even studying in Malaysia.

items.title: Anwar says Malaysia, Maldives to expand cooperation in maritime security, halal and haj
items.summary: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that as a maritime nation, the Maldives placed particular importance on maritime cooperation, including security and training. On Islamic affairs, Anwar said the Maldives’ status as an Islamic country provided opportunities to deepen cooperation in areas including halal, dakwah, Muslim affairs, waqf and haj. “Today we witnessed the exchange of new cooperation agreements in two important areas, which are defence cooperation and Islamic faith.

items.title: Muhyiddin trial: Prosecution completes case after 29 witnesses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — The prosecution today completed its case in former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin's power abuse trial after calling in 29 prosecution witnesses, which means that the trial will now move on to the next stage. Lead prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin this afternoon told the High Court that the prosecution closes its case, and that the prosecution will offer six witnesses that Muhyiddin could call in as his witnesses if he is ordered to defend himself in this case. "With that, the prosecution closes this case.

items.title: Danish PM slams 'reckless action' of Russian frigate firing flares
items.summary: COPENHAGEN: A Russian warship has fired two emergency flares at a Danish helicopter in the Baltic Sea, with the Russian ambassador summoned over the incident, Denmark officials said on Tuesday. The frigate had fired "two flares towards the helicopter. Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen slammed the incident as "reckless action from Russia."

items.title: Four of seven missing anglers found safe off Sekinchan, search continues for three
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 15 — Four of the seven anglers reported missing yesterday were found safe by a local fishing boat in the waters off Sekinchan, 25 nautical miles from the coast of Sungai Besar, at about 9.50 am today. Selangor Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) director Abdul Muhaimin Muhammad Salleh said the four men were found floating close to one another and were in a weak condition. He said the search and rescue operation was ongoing to locate the remaining three victims, with the maritime search area expanded to 203.5 square nautical miles, while the aerial search covers 764 square nautical miles.

items.title: KL police propose KK Mart stores as Go-To-Safety-Point locations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Kuala Lumpur police have proposed making KK Mart convenience stores Go-To-Safety-Point (GTSP) locations as part of a strategic collaboration to strengthen crime monitoring and prevention efforts in the capital. City police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said his team has identified around 700 KK Mart branches in Kuala Lumpur and Selangor that operate 24 hours, have bright lighting, and are equipped with centralised closed-circuit television (CCTV) systems, which have the potential to be safe locations for the public to seek assistance during emergencies. Meanwhile, Fadil said that the KK Mart branch at the Kuala Lumpur police headquarters is the first convenience store branch in the police building.

items.title: What makes us proud to be Malaysian: Peace, unity and hope
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Peace, unity in diversity and a shared hope for a better future are among the things Malaysians say make them proud of their country as they mark the 63rd Malaysia Day tomorrow. "Malaysia is also unique because it has various races and communities living together. God willing, Malaysia will continue forward as a prestigious country," he said.

items.title: Mahmoud Khalil sues Columbia for alleged failure to protect pro-Palestinian students
items.summary: NEW YORK: Mahmoud Khalil and other pro-Palestinian student activists sued Columbia University on Monday, accusing the Ivy League school of being deliberately indifferent to years of pervasive harassment because of their advocacy. The complaint filed in Manhattan federal court by Khalil, the SIPA Palestine Working Group and its president, Mohammad Zubairi, said Columbia violated federal civil rights law through its failure to protect students from threats, doxxing and other harassment based on their perceived Arab or Muslim ancestry, or their advocacy for Palestinian rights. At a press conference at Columbia announcing the lawsuit, Khalil said the university exhibited a "rotten, institutionalised anti-Palestinian bigotry" entrenched in every department and backed by its board of trustees.

items.title: Muhyiddin grateful for acquittal, hopes to be freed on remaining charges
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin said he felt vindicated by the High Court's decision to acquit him of four of seven charges linked to the Jana Wibawa programme. Muhyiddin, who expressed gratitude to God following the decision, said the acquittal brought him a sense of relief after maintaining all along that he was not guilty. "I thank God for the decision.

items.title: Haze: Johan Setia records highest API at 188, 47 stations remain unhealthy [WATCH]
items.summary: Shah Alam recorded 173, while Seremban and Tangkak each recorded 172. Kuala Selangor in Selangor, Temerloh and Jerantut in Pahang recorded 163 each, while Balok Baru Kuantan recorded 162. Port Dickson in Negeri Sembilan recorded 159, while Paka in Terengganu recorded 158.

items.title: Indonesia records 1,437 hotspots as transboundary haze persists
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia recorded 1,437 high‑confidence hotspots as of Monday night, with Kalimantan accounting for the bulk of detections as transboundary haze persisted across the region. Indonesia's Forestry Ministry official Lusiana Martapuri said Central Kalimantan recorded the highest concentration with 689 hotspots, followed by West Kalimantan with 203, South Sumatra 116, South Kalimantan 112 and Jambi nine. No high‑confidence hotspots were detected in Riau, she said, adding that firefighting efforts are focused mainly on Kalimantan, particularly Central and West Kalimantan.

items.title: SMK Ghafar Baba tops DRB-HICOM-Harian Metro Melaka pantun competition
items.summary: BANDA HILIR: SMK Ghafar Baba emerged as champion of the 2026 DRB-HICOM-Harian Metro Proverb-themed Pantun Competition at the Melaka state level yesterday. Also present were Harian Metro Group editor Husain Jahit, Dewan Bahasa dan Pustaka (DBP) Language and Literature Development Department director Abang Haliman Abang Julai, Melaka Education Department director Mahfudzah Mohamed Noor and SMK Tinggi Melaka principal Johan Othman. SMK Ghafar Baba clinched the title through the performances of four contestants — Putera Hirfan Abdullah, Muhammad Hasif Muhammad Fazlie, Muhammad Hafiy Iskandar Mohd Hazri and Nur Aisyy Humairah Mohd Rajab.

items.title: From barefoot schoolboy to chief justice: Remembering Eusoff Chin
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: He walked barefoot to school, sold his mother's kuih at a railway station during the Japanese occupation and studied beneath streetlights because there was no proper light at home. Decades later, Tun Mohd Eusoff Chin rose to become the country's second chief justice. But to his youngest daughter, Zuliana Eusoff, the man who reached the pinnacle of the judiciary remained simply a gentle father who never allowed the stature of his office to define him.

items.title: Babysitter pleads not guilty to exposing toddler to conditions that could have caused death
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 15 — A babysitter pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to a charge of exposing a 13-month-old boy under her care to conditions that could have caused his death last week. Noraidah Khairuddin, 44, entered the plea after the charge was read out before Judge Irwan Suainbon. According to the charge, Noraidah, as a person having custody of the toddler, was accused of exposing him in a manner that could have caused his death.

items.title: KL police propose KK Mart stores as safety points to boost crime prevention
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — The Kuala Lumpur Police propose making KK Mart convenience stores as Go-To-Safety-Point (GTSP) locations through a strategic collaboration with the company to strengthen crime monitoring and prevention efforts in the capital. “We see that KK Mart can be made a safety point for the surrounding community. Meanwhile, Fadil said that the KK Mart branch at the Kuala Lumpur IPK is the first convenience store branch in the PDRM building.

items.title: Pesta Pulau Pinang to continue at new venue
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The Penang government will continue Pesta Pulau Pinang this year, with Padang Menora being considered as the new venue after the festival lost its long-time site at the Sungai Nibong fairground. Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the state was considering the venue in collaboration with the Penang Regional Development Authority (Perda), which had offered the site. "The state government has indeed planned to continue Pesta Pulau Pinang from this year, but we can no longer use the Sungai Nibong fairground for the event.

items.title: NADA to station officers at RTS Link entry points from Dec 31
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The National Anti-Drugs Agency (NADA) will station officers from its Anti-Drugs Border Unit (UAS) at the two entry points of the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link ahead of its operation on Dec 31. NADA director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh said the officers would be stationed at the Bukit Chagar Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security (ICQS) Complex in Johor and the Woodlands North Customs, Immigration and Quarantine (CIQ) Complex in Singapore. He said the matter was among those discussed during a bilateral meeting between NADA and Singapore's Central Narcotics Bureau (CNB) in the capital today.

items.title: MACC officer withdraws police report against Muhyiddin's lawyer
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officer has withdrawn a police report against Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin's lawyer over an issue raised during the Bersatu president's Jana Wibawa trial. MACC investigating officer Mazery Mohd Zaini said his assistant withdrew the report at 12.45pm today. Mazery said this during Muhyiddin's Jana Wibawa trial before High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin.

items.title: Company owner, car broker on remand for probe into falsification of vehicle ownership documents
items.summary: IPOH: A company owner and a car broker are on remand for seven days until Sept 21 to assist in an investigation into a syndicate allegedly falsifying vehicle ownership documents at a local enforcement agency. According to a source from the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), the two men, in their 30s and 40s, respectively, are suspected of bribing officers at the agency to alter vehicle ownership records. The arrests followed the MACC's uncovering of the syndicate's activities in collaboration with the Road Transport Department (RTD), which allegedly involved falsifying vehicle ownership documents to facilitate changes in ownership status.

items.title: Enforcement agency personnel among four remanded over animal feed claims
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: An enforcement agency personnel was among four people remanded for five days for allegedly submitting false documents in claims involving the supply of animal feed worth RM1.8 million. Magistrate Aina Azahra Ariffin ordered the four to be remanded until Saturday (Sept 19) following a MACC application at the magistrate's court today. A source said the suspects, comprising three men and a woman aged between 40 and 60, were detained at about 9pm yesterday after appearing at the Kuala Lumpur MACC office to give statements.

items.title: A-GC moves to block judicial review of 2024 diesel subsidy removal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) has objected to an application by two men seeking leave for a judicial review of the government's decision to remove and rationalise diesel subsidies in Peninsular Malaysia in June 2024. Senior federal counsel Mohammad Sallehuddin Md Ali contended that the decision to end the subsidies cannot be challenged through judicial review, as the matter is not governed by any written law. The application for leave to commence judicial review was filed on Oct 7, 2024, by Azhani Marlan @ Abd Halim, 49, and Mohd Hatta Sanuri, 50.

items.title: 80.35kg syabu disguised as 'tofu cat litter' seized in Bintulu
items.summary: Sarawak Customs director Datuk Norizan Haji Yahya said the seizure was carried out by the Bintulu Enforcement Branch in collaboration with the Narcotics Branch and Intelligence Branch at the department's headquarters. He said officers began monitoring several packages addressed to a premises in Bintulu on Aug 28. He said subsequent inspection found that the packages contained methamphetamine.

items.title: Joint commission meet with Maldives proposed in Kuala Lumpur by year-end
items.summary: MALÉ: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has proposed that the Malaysia-Maldives Joint Commission meet in Kuala Lumpur by the end of the year, signalling a push to accelerate bilateral cooperation and resolve outstanding issues between the two countries. Anwar said the commission was "very, very critical," particularly as several matters remained unresolved, and that an early meeting would demonstrate both countries' commitment to strengthening their bilateral ties. Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan and Malaysian High Commissioner to Sri Lanka and the Maldives Badli Hisham Adam were also present.

items.title: Anwar moots Malaysia-Maldives joint commission in KL this year
items.summary: MALÉ, Sept 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has proposed convening the Malaysia-Maldives Joint Commission in Kuala Lumpur before the end of this year to further advance bilateral relations between the two countries. Anwar said the Commission would be an important platform to address outstanding issues and translate the close relationship between Malaysia and the Maldives into concrete cooperation. Anwar said the Commission could also address issues affecting Maldivians in Malaysia, including students and those seeking healthcare.

items.title: Anwar praises Maldivian president for taking principled stand on Palestine
items.summary: MALÉ: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim praised Maldivian President Dr Mohamed Muizzu for taking a principled stand on the Palestinian issue, saying Malaysia and the Maldives shared broadly similar foreign policy positions, particularly on Gaza. He said both countries remained deeply concerned over the humanitarian crisis in Gaza, where the killings and destruction of Palestinians had continued despite calls for human rights and democracy by the international community. He said the international community must also confront the issue of colonisation in Palestine, noting that countries which had fought against colonialism were now reluctant to speak out against Israel's occupation of Palestinian land.

items.title: People advised against rushing to replace MyKad from Sept 17
items.summary: Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the replacement exercise for the new MyKad, which comes with about 50 additional security features, would be carried out in phases, while existing cards would remain valid for daily transactions. "I would like to advise people not to rush to replace their MyKad. He said the replacement of the MyKad would not affect subsidy balances or eligibility for subsidies linked to the identity card.

items.title: Pahang litterbugs plead to avoid community service
items.summary: The offenders, including civil servants and professionals, have attempted to negotiate with the Solid Waste Management and Public Cleansing Corporation (SWCorp), with some even offering to pay a higher fine instead of performing community service. SWCorp Pahang director Cairul Hisham Jalaluddin said a total of 3,295 notices had been issued across Pahang between Jan 1 and Sept 14 this year, with about 200 offenders ordered to perform community service. The programme today involved 22 offenders performing community service in four districts — Kuantan, Bera, Pekan and Temerloh.

items.title: GOF seizes smuggled cigarettes worth over RM1.9mil in Klang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The General Operations Force (GOF) seized various types of smuggled cigarettes, worth over RM1.9 million, in a raid on a premises in Bandar Bukit Raja, Klang yesterday. He said that during the raid, the police arrested a 52-year-old man who was suspected of being the courier for the untaxed cigarettes supply. As a result of the raid, the police seized a total of 4,920 cartons of various types and brands of untaxed cigarettes.

items.title: Residential projects built in Melaka to undergo selling price valuation review
items.summary: MELAKA: The state government will ensure that every new development, especially residential projects built in Melaka, undergoes a review of the selling price valuation before the project is implemented. Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said the review will be conducted by the Valuation and Property Services Department (JPPH) through the State Land Subdivision and Partition Committee. "The proof, Alhamdulillah, based on the National Property Information Centre Report for the first quarter of this year, Melaka recorded the lowest house sale prices in Malaysia," he said.

items.title: Police open to helping MOH operate mercy flights
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The police are open to helping the Health Ministry (MOH) operate mercy flights to transport patients requiring emergency treatment from remote areas. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail, however, said the air operations force currently faced constraints in terms of available air assets, given the vast operational area it covered nationwide. He said the police currently had only two fixed-wing aircraft and one helicopter available in Sarawak.

items.title: Don’t rush: Home minister urges Malaysians to avoid MyKad replacement frenzy
items.summary: PORT DICKSON, Sept 15 — The people have been advised not to rush to replace their MyKad when applications for the new version open on Sept 17, to avoid congestion at National Registration Department (NRD) offices. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the replacement exercise for the new MyKad, which comes with about 50 additional security features, would be carried out in phases, while existing cards would remain valid for daily transactions. “I would like to advise people not to rush to replace their MyKad.

items.title: Malaysia must strengthen care economy to boost women's workforce participation - Nancy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia must strengthen its care economy to help more women enter or return to the workforce, said Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri. Delivering her keynote address at the 5th Malaysia Sustainability Leadership Summit today, she said 42.8 per cent of the 4.89 million women outside the labour force cited domestic responsibilities and caregiving as their main reason for staying out of the workforce. Hence, women's economic participation remains a major opportunity," she said.

items.title: Fahmi presents Malaysia Day invitation to Sarawak governor
items.summary: KUCHING: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil today paid a courtesy call on Sarawak Governor Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar to present an official invitation to the Malaysia Day celebration at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) tomorrow night. Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah and I presented the invitation to Tun for tomorrow's celebration. Also present were Sarawak Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister and Minister-in-Charge of the Malaysia Day 2026 celebration Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah, and Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah.

items.title: Prosecution drops four charges against Muhyiddin, presses on with three in corruption trial
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — The High Court today acquitted former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin of four charges involving Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd's funds, as the prosecution today said it does not want to proceed with trial on those charges for now. In this trial, Muhyiddin faced seven charges: four counts of alleged power abuse to obtain RM225.3 million in bribes for his party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd), and three counts of alleged money laundering involving money that Bersatu received from Bukhary Equity. Following the High Court's decision after the prosecution's request for a discharge not amounting to acquittal (DNAA), Muhyiddin now only faces three power abuse charges involving RM25.3 million in alleged bribes for his party Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia.

items.title: Ipsos poll: Malaysians prioritise jobs and homes over traditional milestones
items.summary: Specifically, 67 per cent of Malaysians identify a stable job as essential, compared to 65 per cent globally, while 60 per cent view home ownership as a key milestone, slightly above the global average of 58 per cent. Parenthood and marriage are viewed as markers of success by 47 per cent and 42 per cent of Malaysians, respectively, far outpacing global figures of 31 per cent and 25 per cent. Home ownership follows closely, cited by 64 per cent of Millennials and 55 per cent of Gen Z.

items.title: Muhyiddin trial: Lawyer accuses MACC officer of ‘intimidation’ over police report
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad today told the High Court that a Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officer had allegedly attempted to intimidate and tarnish his reputation as a lawyer, based on the officer’s MACC colleague’s police report. Amer, who was cross-examining MACC officer Mazery Mohd Zaini as the 29th prosecution witness yesterday in Muhyiddin’s power abuse trial, said the police report had false information. Amer said the police report lodged yesterday had named him and referred to the ongoing trial, and referred to an alleged classified document that Muhyiddin’s lawyers had wanted to be included as evidence in the trial.

items.title: Police receive two reports over Negeri Sembilan MB’s alleged forced signing of royal document
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 15 — Police have received two reports concerning the Proclamation document allegedly signed under duress by Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim, seeking to remove the 11th Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said following the reports lodged by the Menteri Besar, the police would classify the case to determine the appropriate direction and scope of the investigation. “I can confirm that two police reports were lodged by the Menteri Besar. It is our duty, upon receiving the reports, to classify them based on the nature and direction of the investigation.

items.title: Pesta Pulau Pinang returns, but moves to Tasek Gelugor after 50 Years at Sungai Nibong
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 15 — Pesta Pulau Pinang will return this year for a month-long celebration starting December 1, with the event relocating to Padang Menora in Tasek Gelugor. Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow confirmed that while the annual event continues as scheduled, it will be held at a more compact venue compared to its traditional site in Sungai Nibong. The state government had explored several alternative locations before the Penang Regional Development Authority (Perda) offered the Tasek Gelugor site.

items.title: Fadhlina urges parents to screen children early for autism, ADHD and learning difficulties
items.summary: GUA MUSANG, Sept 15 — The Ministry of Education (MOE) is encouraging parents to bring their children for screening programmes aimed at detecting learning difficulties, including autism spectrum disorder and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), at an early stage. Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the screening programmes are crucial to ensuring children with learning difficulties receive appropriate intervention and support. Fadhlina said the services include speech therapy and psychological assessments to evaluate children’s overall development.

items.title: Anwar receives 21-gun salute as Maldives rolls out red carpet for Malaysian PM
items.summary: MALE, Sept 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was accorded a full ceremonial welcome here today, marking the start of his official programme during his two-day visit to the Maldives. The Prime Minister, who is also Finance Minister, was accompanied by Maldives Minister of Islamic Affairs Dr Mohamed Shaheem Ali Saeed, who is the minister-in-attendance for the visit. Also present at the welcoming ceremony were Malaysian Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan and Malaysian High Commissioner to Sri Lanka and the Maldives Badli Hisham Adam.

items.title: Two detained after KPDN foils 2,400-litre diesel misappropriation attempt in Senai
items.summary: Johor KPDN director Lilis Saslinda Pornomo said the operation followed information and intelligence on diesel purchases suspected of violating the Control of Supplies Act 1961. Enforcement personnel found a suspicious lorry equipped with a storage tank and related equipment, filling diesel directly into the tank. KPDN also seized 15 fleet cards and five receipts or invoices related to the fuel purchases,” Lilis Saslinda said in a statement.

items.title: Police nab two ex-convicts in Johor over 11 cases involving housebreaking, robbery and theft
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Sept 15 — Two ex-convicts who were released three years ago have been rearrested for their alleged involvement in 11 separate criminal cases, including housebreaking, robbery and theft, in the district recently. Iskandar Puteri acting police chief Superintendent Saifullah Jaya @ Yahaya said the two male suspects, aged 26 and 27, were arrested in the Tanjung Kupang and Kangkar Pulai areas on Sept 5. He said the arrests were made following a police report lodged on Sept 4 regarding a break-in at Forest City Starview in Gelang Patah.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng’s call to drop Umno from Penang govt not DAP stance, says Chow Kon Yeow
items.summary: BATU KAWAN, Sept 15 — Penang Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Chow Kon Yeow stressed that DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng’s call for Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi to urge Penang PH to drop Umno from the state government does not represent the party’s official position. “It is not the party’s position (Lim Guan Eng’s challenge to Ahmad Zahid). Earlier, Guan Eng challenged Ahmad Zahid to urge Penang PH to drop Umno from the state government.

items.title: Former construction manager claims trial over RM14,000 CBT involving Tabung Haji project
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 15 — A former construction project manager pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to a charge of criminal breach of trust (CBT) involving penalty collection totalling RM14,000 from a contractor for a commercial building project owned by Lembaga Tabung Haji. Mohamad Hashim Mukhatap, 53, then the Construction Manager for THP Timur Sdn Bhd, was charged with misappropriating the funds—collected as penalties from the contractor, Kelpile Sdn Bhd—by depositing them into his personal bank account. The case involves a proposed project to construct and complete a 22-storey commercial building comprising serviced apartments (244 units), penthouses (four units), public amenities, commercial space, parking facilities, a sub-basement (one level), and related facilities on Lot 273, Section 12, Kota Bharu.

items.title: Four Chinese nationals claim trial over alleged kidnapping of woman in Alor Setar
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Sept 15 — Three men and a woman, all of Chinese nationality, pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to a charge of kidnapping a fellow national last month. Huang Jian, 39; Wang Hao Yu, 33; Guan Siqi, 24; and Liu Tingjun, 46, entered their pleas after the charge was read out to them in Mandarin before Judge N. Priscilla Hemamalini. Deputy Public Prosecutor Nasruna Anhar Nordien appeared for the prosecution, while Guan Siqi was represented by lawyer S. Suresh, and the other three accused by lawyer Jodia Poh Yi Tying.

items.title: Queen Raja Zarith Sofiah orders postponement of Johor Family Day Carnival amid worsening haze
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 15 — Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, yesterday instructed that the Johor Family Day Carnival, scheduled for Sept 16, be postponed to a suitable date following the worsening haze situation in the state. According to a post uploaded on the Facebook page of Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar, Her Majesty instructed that the carnival be held when air quality improves. Insya-Allah, this carnival will be held when air quality returns to a good level,” Her Majesty said.

items.title: Dzulkefly: 902 health clinics nationwide to offer AI-assisted lung screening by year-end
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — A total of 902 health clinics nationwide will be empowered with Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted lung disease screening by the end of this year, said Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad. He said the step to strengthen lung health is crucial given that respiratory diseases currently account for one in five deaths globally. In this regard, Dr Dzulkefly praised the decade-long contributions of the NIHR Global Health Research Unit on Respiratory Health (RESPIRE) in driving public health research.

items.title: Malaysia Day H-series plate bidding opens tomorrow, numbers from 1 to 9,999 up for grabs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Bidding for the special H-series vehicle registration numbers in conjunction with Malaysia Day will open on Wednesday and run until Sept 20, offering numbers from 1 to 9,999. He said the H series is special as the last single-letter series JPJ will offer, while also symbolising harmony in conjunction with Malaysia Day celebrations. Aedy Fadly said the H series differed from taxi registrations, where the letter H must be accompanied by a state registration letter.

items.title: Azalina pushes questions on Najib’s pardon bid to Hannah Yeoh, says BHEUU is just the messenger
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Questions surrounding the deferment of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's royal pardon petition should be directed to Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, says Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. The minister for law and institutional reform said that she does not sit as the executive representative on the Federal Territories Pardons Board, noting that the Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) under her purview functions strictly as the board's administrative secretariat, NST reported. "BHEUU is under me, but for the Pardons Board in each state, BHEUU is the secretariat, while the minister and menteri besar of the respective state are the executive representatives on the board.

items.title: Haniff Khatri and family escape unhurt as pre-dawn blaze damages three homes in Gombak (VIDEO)
items.summary: Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Assistant Director of Operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency distress call regarding the blaze at 3.06am, Sinar Harian reported. “A total of 15 firefighters and officers from the Rawang Fire and Rescue Station (BBP), assisted by the Batu Arang Fire and Rescue Station, together with fire engines, were deployed to the scene, which is located about eight kilometres away,” he said today. “The estimated damage caused by the fire was 80 per cent to the first house, 20 per cent to the second house, and five per cent to the third house,” he said.

items.title: Four boys drown after falling into deep drain while trying to retrieve football in Kulim
items.summary: KULIM, Sept 15 — Four boys died after allegedly falling into a drain while attempting to retrieve a football at Taman Desa Kayangan, Sungai Karangan, yesterday evening. Kulim police Chief Supt Syamsul Sinring said two of the victims died at the scene, while the other two succumbed to their injuries while being taken to Kulim Hospital. Syamsul said all four victims lived near Taman Desa Kayangan.

items.title: Fahmi says Malaysia Day preparations in Kuching on track, internet access for media assured
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 15 — Final preparations for the 2026 Malaysia Day celebrations at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) are at a satisfactory level, including the provision of internet facilities for media practitioners. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said an inspection with senior ministry officers tonight found that preparations for the celebration tomorrow were progressing well. Also present were Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah and Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) chief executive officer Datin Paduka Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin.

items.title: Unity minister condemns Umno assembly joke on Catholic clergy, urges authorities to act
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang has denounced a controversial remark made during the Umno General Assembly 2026 that used Catholic priests and nuns as the subject of a joke, warning that such conduct crosses a line that must not be tolerated in Malaysia's multi-religious society. In a media statement today, Dagang said he views the controversy seriously, stressing that jokes touching on religious institutions, religious figures, holy texts or the beliefs of any community are never acceptable, regardless of the intent behind them. Dagang argued that freedom of speech and political expression do not give anyone licence to trample on the religious sensitivities of others, and said this principle must be applied evenly regardless of religion, race, status or political affiliation.

items.title: Anwar defends moderate approach on Umno ties, says govt stability must come first
items.summary: KERALAM, Sept 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has chosen a moderate approach in handling differing views regarding the issue of cooperation with Umno within the Unity Government. Anwar, who is also Pakatan Harapan (PH) Chairman, stated that the government must remain stable because any overly harsh actions concerning the issue could result in losses for the country. Elaborating further, Anwar said various views were also voiced among political parties including PH, but such matters are normal within a coalition and should not be seen as something that could threaten government cooperation.

items.title: Anwar says Miti to pursue wider market access for Malaysian goods in India
items.summary: KERALAM, Sept 15 — The Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (MITI) will follow up on efforts to widen access for Malaysian goods to the Indian market, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said the matter was discussed during his meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi, with several restrictions still needing to be addressed to facilitate trade between the two countries. He said the matter was also raised during his meeting with Keralam Chief Minister V.D.
